editorial:
Imagine walking into a TV studio where Elmer Fudd is trying to be a professional host, but everything is falling apart. You get to see Bugs Bunny as the star of the show, looking back at all his old tricks and pranks. The vibe is pure chaos, especially because Daffy Duck is there, absolutely hating every second of Bugs getting all the attention. It is a total blast to watch the dynamic between these three, and you will love how Granny keeps Daffy in line with a few well-timed hits on the head whenever he gets too loud.

What really makes this work is the way it uses old clips to tell a story, which keeps the pacing fast and funny. The comedy is timeless, though some of the gags are very simple. If you love classic slapstick, this is right up your alley. Since it is a short, it is a great way to unwind. You should definitely look for a restored version to get the best colors. Whether you are streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or adding a 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection, the crisp picture makes the animation pop.
endingExplained: The short wraps up with the show becoming a complete disaster. After seeing all the clips of Bugs winning, Daffy finally loses his mind from jealousy. The tension peaks when the characters stop pretending to be on a polite TV show and go back to their usual fighting. It ends with the classic Looney Tunes style of mayhem, leaving you laughing as the credits roll on the chaotic celebration of Bugs Bunny's life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic Looney Tunes and slapstick humor.
